reasons.packages/broker/src/developer/server.ts: signin.session_started (authorizationCodeGrant, createSession(redeemed)), signin.refresh_grace and signin.session_revoked (revoke) log a sign-in session that a refresh token reaches. Those are code-grant sessions of the CLI or a registered client: CodeGrant has no reviewExpiresAt, so authenticateDeveloperSessionId refuses them as a cookie. A browser review session (createSession with reviewExpiresAt, same file) discards its refresh token, so no presentable token reaches revoke or the refresh grant for it, and its signin.browser_succeeded line carries no id. Fragile by construction: if a browser session ever gains a refresh token this entry is wrong.
reasons.packages/broker/src/developer/canary-ses: signin.canary_session: a canary session mints amr github with no reviewExpiresAt (mintSession in this file), so authenticateDeveloperSessionId refuses the id as a cookie; the signed token is the credential. The file is added by the canary-session lane; an entry for a file that does not exist yet is harmless (the ratchet only refuses a count above the allowance).

escapeReasons.packages/cli/src/deploy/commands.ts: createInterface({ output: process.stderr }): readline prompt output for a person at a terminal, no log entry; writes through the stream cannot carry a session id (the CLI holds no browser session)

escapeReasons.packages/cli/src/main.ts: process.stdout and process.stderr handed to the command handlers as `stdout`/`stderr` dependencies (and one `.write` on the dependency); a `.write` on a name `stdout` or `stderr` is still scanned by this test, so a session id written through them is caught
